reason: council-remediation-2026-07-20/agent-P override. The currently linked question's marked-correct option B ('3 meters') and rationale ('RA 7279 designates areas within 3 meters of esteros as danger zones where occupants may be evicted without permanent resettlement being required first') are factually wrong on two counts: (1) RA 7279 does NOT specify a 3-meter distance threshold for danger areas; the 3-meter figure derives from PD 1067's urban easement. RA 7279 Section 28 lists danger areas by type (esteros, riverbanks, shorelines, etc.) without a numeric setback. (2) RA 7279 does NOT waive relocation in danger areas; Section 29 requires LGUs with NHA to provide relocation with basic services and livelihood access. The article body of lea-plan-003-01 explicitly excludes 'eviction-distance rules' from its scope and the article body of lea-plan-003-06 confirms relocation is required.

source_audit_support.source_locator: RA 7279 Section 28 (lists danger areas by type, no numeric setback) and Section 29 (LGU + NHA relocation duty); PD 1067 Article 51 (3m urban easement is a separate Water Code rule, not an RA 7279 danger-area threshold). Article body lea-plan-003-01 normalized.md last paragraph: 'Do not import... eviction-distance rules unless a separately audited source is provided.'

proposed.text: Which of the following areas is listed as a DANGER AREA under RA 7279 (Urban Development and Housing Act), Section 28, where eviction may be lawful?

options.text: Esteros, railroad tracks, garbage dumps, riverbanks, shorelines, waterways, and other public places where occupation poses danger to life and property.
Any private residential subdivision built before 1992, regardless of physical hazard.
Any land within 50 kilometers of an active fault line, with no other condition.
Any land owned by a government-owned or controlled corporation, regardless of hazard.

rationale.a: Correct. RA 7279 Section 28 lists danger areas by type: esteros, railroad tracks, garbage dumps, riverbanks, shorelines, waterways, and other public places where the occupation poses danger to life and property. The statute does not specify a numeric setback; specific distances come from other codes (e.g., PD 1067 easements).
rationale.b: Wrong. RA 7279 does not classify all pre-1992 subdivisions as danger areas.
rationale.c: Wrong. RA 7279 does not impose a 50-kilometer fault-line buffer. Fault setbacks come from PHIVOLCS guidance (5-meter minimum) and CLUP integration, not from RA 7279.
rationale.d: Wrong. Government ownership alone does not make land a danger area under RA 7279; the listed physical hazards do.
rationale.correct: RA 7279 Section 28 enumerates danger areas by physical type. Numeric setback distances are not in RA 7279 itself; they come from related codes such as PD 1067. Section 28 safeguards and Section 29 relocation still apply even in danger-area evictions.
rationale.takeaway: Do not attach a '3-meter' figure to RA 7279 danger areas. RA 7279 lists danger areas by type; numeric easements come from PD 1067 (Water Code) and other codes.

proposed.explanation: Article body lea-plan-003-01: 'Do not import... eviction-distance rules unless a separately audited source is provided.' RA 7279 Section 28 lists danger areas by type; PD 1067 supplies numeric easements by land classification.
